page_title: A field guide to Claude Fable 5: Finding your unknowns

sources.entry: A Field Guide to Claude Fable 5 by Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic - Really solid, insightful guidance on working/thinking with Claude Fable, and with AI in general. Very well written. Hints of Rumsfeld epistemology, but otherwise it's a great piece.

summary.name: A field guide to Claude Fable 5: Finding your unknowns
summary.one_liner: An Anthropic blog article by Thariq Shihipar describing a method for finding unknowns (missing context and decisions) before, during, and after working with Claude Code on Claude Fable 5.
keywords: how to prompt ai coding agent
use_cases: preparing a prompt for an AI coding agent
learning an unfamiliar domain with an AI assistant
creating a pitch or explainer doc for reviewers
prototyping UI designs with an AI model
summary.what_it_does: The article frames the gap between what a user tells an AI agent (the map) and the real constraints of the work (the territory) as unknowns. It splits unknowns into known knowns, known unknowns, unknown knowns, and unknown unknowns. It then lists working patterns: a blind spot pass, brainstorming and prototyping, being interviewed by Claude, pointing it at reference source code, and writing implementation plans. During implementation it suggests keeping an implementation-notes file for deviations. After implementation it suggests pitch docs and quizzes on the changes. Example prompts are given for each pattern, and the author describes using Claude Code to edit a launch video.
notable: Introduces a four-way taxonomy of unknowns (known knowns, known unknowns, unknown knowns, unknown unknowns)
Gives concrete example prompts for each stage: blind spot pass, brainstorm, interview, reference, plan, implementation notes, quiz
Written by an Anthropic team member, based on the author's own Claude Code workflow
caveats: This is a written guide, not a software tool, so it has no pricing or download
Advice is based on the author's personal workflow and is not presented as a formal method
